statement.p: Calculate the integral, if it converges. If it diverges, enter diverges for your answer.

static.solution: 1/v is undefined at v=0. To evaluate it, we must split the region of integration up into two pieces, from 0 to 4 and from -4 to 0. But notice, \int_0^{4}{1\over v}\, dv = \lim_{b\to 0^+}\int_b^{4} {1\over v}\, dv = \lim_{b\to 0^+}\left({\ln v}\bigg|_b^{4}\right) = \ln(4) - \ln b. As b\to 0^+, this goes to infinity and the integral diverges, so our original integral also diverges.
